verdict.rationale: Lambda's own docs say every On-Demand Cloud instance comes with a preinstalled JupyterLab server, opened from the Instances page in the console. That delivers the 'open Jupyter in one step' half of the story, and a community user confirms working in Jupyter on a Lambda instance. Connecting an IDE is only implied through SSH access with console-managed keys; there is no documented VS Code or Cursor integration. Missing for 10: documented one-step VS Code/Cursor remote connection, explicit description of the Jupyter launch flow (e.g., a one-click button), independent hands-on detail on IDE connectivity.

support.subject: As a developer, I can open Jupyter or connect my IDE (VS Code/Cursor) to the instance in one step

citations.quote: each ODC instance provides a JupyterLab installation for creating and managing Jupyter notebooks. You can access your instance's JupyterLab by visiting the Instances page
You can connect to your On-Demand Cloud (ODC) instances directly through SSH or by using the preinstalled JupyterLab server.
If you don't have an SSH key, you can generate one in the Lambda Cloud console.
